headline: High-risk filesystem and shell interaction: Open Interpreter can modify the user machine while the paired awesome-nlp list offers no isolation or safeguards.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Open Interpreter reads clipboard/files and can act on content as instructions, while awesome-nlp is a docs-only repository with no runtime isolation or provenance controls. The pair has a plausible manual-copy or file-based bridge, but no direct shared channel is documented, so this is below high.
conditions: IF content from awesome-nlp is copied into Open Interpreter as task text or files
IF Open Interpreter is run with auto-run or equivalent confirmation bypass
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable auto-run in Open Interpreter
Review copied content before pasting into Open Interpreter
Use read-only exports from awesome-nlp
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: Open Interpreter can read the entire local filesystem and has broad network egress, so any sensitive local data reachable on the machine can be exposed through its outputs or model-provider calls. awesome-nlp itself touches no data, but pairing it with a local automation agent on the same machine creates a default leakage path from local files into the agent context.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present on the same machine Open Interpreter can read
IF Open Interpreter is configured to send prompts or file contents to a remote model provider
mitigations: Run Open Interpreter in a dedicated user account
Restrict filesystem access to a narrow project directory
Remove secrets from the machine before use
Use a local-only model provider
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Open Interpreter has write_filesystem, execute_shell, and modify_git_state, while awesome-nlp is a repository artifact that can be used as shared content or a workspace target. Because Open Interpreter shares state via filesystem and supports multiple instances, concurrent writes or git mutations can collide by default; uncertainty about the exact workspace only increases concern, not lowers it.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory or git repository
IF Open Interpreter is allowed to modify files or git state without external locking
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Disable git mutation in Open Interpreter
Commit or stash changes before switching agents
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared workspaces

D_cascading_error.rationale: Open Interpreter can take actions from its own outputs, so if it consumes content derived from awesome-nlp as authoritative instructions or facts, errors can cascade into shell commands or file edits. awesome-nlp provides no verification layer, and Open Interpreter's confirmation flow is bypassable with auto-run, so the interaction is plausible in default use but not inherently catastrophic.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter treats content sourced from awesome-nlp as authoritative
IF auto-run or equivalent confirmation bypass is enabled
mitigations: Require human review before execution
Cross-check outputs against a second source
Keep auto-run disabled
Limit Open Interpreter to non-destructive commands
requires-engineering: add validation gates before action execution

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented for awesome-nlp, while Open Interpreter can access local files and send prompts to configured model providers. The pair therefore creates a generic compliance exposure only if regulated data is present on the machine; the other agent is not itself a regulated-data processor.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored on the local machine Open Interpreter can read
IF that data is included in prompts or file contents sent to a remote model provider
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the working directory
Use a local-only provider
Separate regulated and non-regulated projects
Review retention settings for the provider
requires-engineering: implement data-class filtering before transmission
